title: Upper limb theory · report dated 17 April 2021
note: TUMS report TestId 19619. The report date is 17 April 2021; this does not independently establish the sitting date.

questions.prompt: What is the action of the brachioradialis?
questions.note: Brachioradialis flexes the elbow, especially with the forearm in mid-pronation.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: In the cubital fossa, which of the following structures located most medially?
questions.note: The main cubital contents lie tendon–artery–median nerve from lateral to medial.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the following muscles rotates arm laterally?
questions.note: Infraspinatus laterally rotates the humerus; the other listed muscles are medial rotators.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The muscle that forms the anterior wall of axillary fossa:
questions.note: Pectoralis major and minor contribute to the anterior axillary wall.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles innervated by Median nerve Except:
questions.note: Adductor pollicis is supplied by the deep ulnar branch; the listed thenar alternatives are median-supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The anterior compartment of the arm innervated by:
questions.note: Musculocutaneous supplies the anterior arm compartment.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the below muscle supply by two nerves.
questions.note: Brachialis usually receives musculocutaneous supply plus a radial contribution to its lateral part.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the below choice is in the clavicle.
questions.note: The conoid tubercle is on the inferior lateral clavicle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the following muscles innervated by ulnar nerve except:
questions.note: The first and second lumbricals are median-supplied; the medial two are ulnar-supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: structures that found in the deltopectoral groove:
questions.note: The deltopectoral groove contains the cephalic vein and deltoid branch of the thoracoacromial artery.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the following muscle is innervated by both the ulnar and median nerves.
questions.note: FDP has anterior interosseous/median supply laterally and ulnar supply medially.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: . This is the strong supinator:
questions.note: Biceps is a powerful supinator, particularly with the elbow flexed.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the below muscles abduct the arm to 90 degree.
questions.note: Middle deltoid fibers are the principal abductors after initiation by supraspinatus.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: This muscle attached to the intertubercular groove:
questions.note: Latissimus inserts into the floor of the groove. Teres major inserts into its medial lip; the source wording is broad, so both floor and lip attachment answers are accepted.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: skin of the superior lateral of the arm innervated by :
questions.note: The superior lateral cutaneous nerve of the arm is an axillary nerve branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the following is not branches from the radial artery.
questions.note: Common palmar digital arteries usually arise from the mainly ulnar superficial arch, not directly from the radial artery.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Axillary nerve innervated one of the below muscles.
questions.note: Axillary nerve supplies deltoid and teres minor.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: . Lateral border of the cubital fossa is:
questions.note: Brachioradialis forms the lateral boundary; pronator teres forms the medial boundary. The supplied mark is corrected.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The long head of the biceps brachii muscle originated from the:
questions.note: Long-head biceps originates at the supraglenoid tubercle/superior labrum; infraglenoid gives origin to long-head triceps. The supplied mark is corrected.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Dorsal tubercle located at one of the following bone.
questions.note: Lister’s dorsal tubercle is on the distal radius.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: . Profounda brachii artery is along with one of the nerve below
questions.note: The profunda brachii accompanies the radial nerve in the radial groove.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: It is action of dorsal interosseous muscle.
questions.note: Dorsal interossei abduct digits; they also flex MCP and extend IP joints. Because the stem does not specify a joint, flexion and extension are accepted as well.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the choice is branches from axillary artery except:
questions.note: Internal thoracic arises from the subclavian artery, not the axillary artery.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The superficial palmar arterial arch is formed primarily by the:
questions.note: The superficial palmar arch is mainly ulnar, with variable radial contribution.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the bellow choice is in the anterior view of the humerus except :
questions.note: The olecranon fossa is posterior; radial and coronoid fossae are anterior.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: This nerve located between brachialis and brachioradialis.
questions.note: Radial nerve enters the cubital region between brachialis and brachioradialis.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All of the bellow nerves derived from posterior cord of the brachial plexus except:
questions.note: Long thoracic nerve arises from C5–7 ventral rami; the other choices arise from the posterior cord.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: .All of these muscles belong to the anterior compartment of forearm except:
questions.note: Supinator belongs to the posterior forearm compartment.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the below structures is located in the depth of the snuffbox.
questions.note: Radial artery passes in the floor of the snuffbox. Superficial radial nerve and cephalic vein lie in its roof.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: .This joint is pivot
questions.note: Proximal and distal radioulnar joints are pivot joints.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: . This muscle attached to the pisiform bone.
questions.note: Flexor carpi ulnaris inserts on the pisiform, with ligamentous continuation distally.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: . Insertion of the triceps brachii muscle is:
questions.note: Triceps inserts on the olecranon.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: .Recurrent radial artery anastomosis with:
questions.note: Radial recurrent anastomoses with radial collateral anterior to the lateral epicondyle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: This tendon located medially of the snuff box.
questions.note: EPL forms the medial boundary; APL and EPB form the lateral boundary.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: .One of the below structures passes posteriorly to the flexor retinaculum at the wrist?
questions.note: Median nerve passes deep to the flexor retinaculum within the carpal tunnel. Ulnar nerve/artery and palmaris longus are superficial.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: . All of the following muscles attach to the medial border of the scapula, except:
questions.note: Teres major originates near the inferior angle/lower lateral border, not the medial border.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: .These structures are located in the quadrate space .
options: axillary nerve and anterior circumflex humeral artery
axillary nerve and sub scapular artery .
axillary nerve and circumflex scapular artery .
. axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery .
questions.note: The quadrangular space transmits axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral vessels. The supplied mark is corrected.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: This is not branches from the median nerve.
questions.note: Posterior interosseous is radial-derived. Anterior interosseous is median-derived.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: . The extensor expansion of the fingers is formed by the tendon from the:
questions.note: Extensor digitorum tendons form the finger extensor expansions, receiving intrinsic muscle contributions.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: One of the below muscles is an initiator abduction of Gleno-humeral joint:
questions.note: Supraspinatus initiates glenohumeral abduction.
questions.subject: anatomy

audit.method: Native text + rendered source inspection; independently reviewed anatomical answers and course-section mapping.
